oidc_jwt.description: A valid bearer JWT presented to the JWT auth login endpoint can be reused until it expires; Vault documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for JWT auth.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method API documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for stateless JWT auth.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without an nbf claim, or platform behavior that does not require nbf, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat absence of nbf enforcement alone as a bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault JWT auth is a stateless bearer-token verifier; the same valid upstream JWT can be submitted multiple times to obtain Vault tokens unless external replay controls are added.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth method API documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for plain JWT auth.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault exposes configurable not_before_leeway and can disable added leeway with -1; acceptance behavior around nbf is governed by role configuration rather than a universal strict policy.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT auth method API documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Future-nbf handling is configuration-sensitive; do not over-interpret acceptance without checking role leeway settings.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until JWKS cache state is refreshed when using remote JWKS or discovery-based validation.
oidc_jwt.source: Standard JWKS caching behavior for JWKS/discovery-based validation
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag old-key acceptance after the relevant cache window or refresh point, not immediately after admin rotation.

oidc_jwt.description: If an admin changes JWT trust configuration such as jwks_url, jwt_validation_pubkeys, or bound_issuer, logins succeeding under the new configuration are expected.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault JWT/OIDC auth method configuration semantics
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance under the newly configured trust anchor as trust-anchor substitution.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider metadata declares request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault OIDC provider discovery response example
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request-object attacks are not applicable to this provider endpoint.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request object tests are not applicable to these endpoints.

oidc_jwt.description: For Vault OIDC providers and named keys, an empty allowed_client_ids list denies all clients; '*' is the explicit allow-all sentinel.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault OIDC provider and identity token key API docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret empty allow-lists as permissive misconfiguration.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider clients allow no Vault entities by default unless assignments are configured; allow_all must be supplied to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault OIDC provider client API docs
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failure through an unassigned client is expected default-deny behavior, not an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth mount-derived prefix before the user identity value.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag mount-prefixed display_name values as identity collisions when the suffix matches the sent identity.

oidc_jwt.constraint: JWT auth config requires exactly one trust source: configure_jwt_validation MUST set one and only one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. jwks_pairs is also mutually exclusive with jwks_url/jwks_ca_pem and bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Misconfiguring these fields causes setup failure rather than a meaningful security result.

Every JWT/OIDC auth role requires at least one bound value. create_auth_role MUST set at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or another documented bound constraint; otherwise role creation/update is invalid and tests will fail before login.

For JWT roles that validate tokens carrying an aud claim, create_auth_role MUST set bound_audiences. Vault documents bound_audiences as required for jwt roles that contain an audience and it must match at least one JWT aud value. Do not run audience-validation tests against a role missing bound_audiences because acceptance/rejection would be misconfigured, not a vulnerability.

bound_subject supports exact string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type parameter. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely if multiple different sub values must authenticate to the same role. Setting bound_subject to '*' matches only the literal string '*'.

bound_audiences is exact membership matching only. There is no companion type parameter for wildcard or glob semantics. For multi-identity or cross-provider tests that need varying aud values to pass the same role, do not set a wildcard string; either configure the exact allowed audience values or omit the constraint when the test requires unconstrained audiences.

bound_claims matching semantics depend on bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means values are treated as literals and must match exactly; '*' is literal, not wildcard. If bound_claims_type='glob', '*' matches any number of characters. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple values to pass the same claim constraint, either omit the exact-match claim constraint or explicitly set bound_claims_type='glob' with an intentional pattern.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string' so numeric JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright as non-string literals.

If testing numeric claim coercion on bound_claims and documentation does not guarantee strict cross-type handling, the fuzzer SHOULD probe truncation/coercion behavior by configuring a numeric bound value N and sending a JWT claim with float N+0.7. Acceptance would indicate unsafe coercion. Use bound_claims with bound_claims_type='glob' so numeric claims are accepted into matching logic rather than rejected before comparison.

Leeway parameters use sentinel values with non-obvious meanings. clock_skew_leeway: value 0 means use default 60 seconds, value -1 means disable extra leeway. expiration_leeway: value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 means disable extra leeway. not_before_leeway: value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 means disable extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero tolerance.

For I2 expired_token tests, do not set expiration_leeway=0 expecting strict expiry. In Vault, 0 selects the default 150-second grace period. To test strict expiration behavior, set expiration_leeway=-1 or a small explicit duration, and use a control token with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}}.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests, do not set not_before_leeway=0 expecting strict enforcement. In Vault, 0 selects the default 150-second grace period. To test strict not-before behavior, set not_before_leeway=-1 or a small explicit duration, and include a control login using a valid token.

For I2 freshness tests, include a control login using a valid JWT alongside any expired or future-dated attack JWT. Recommended control claims: exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub={{jwt_sub}}. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust-anchor or role setup.

token_num_uses and other token use-budget fields count every API call made with the issued Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If token_num_uses=1, lookup-self will exhaust the token before the protected-read check. Minimum safe value for sequences that perform both verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret is 2, and higher if additional session-authenticated calls are made.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and fall back to the mount's default_role. The fuzzer MUST intentionally omit role only when testing default-role behavior; otherwise always send an explicit role to avoid false positives caused by admin changes to default_role.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless jwks_pairs is used. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests would pass trivially due to missing configuration rather than a validation bypass.

For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation to replace jwks_url or jwt_validation_pubkeys, then retry login with the old signing key. Acceptance of the NEW trust anchor after an admin change is by design; only continued acceptance of the OLD key after the change is relevant.
OIDC provider authorization requests require scope to include 'openid' and response_type='code'. Tests that omit openid or use unsupported response types are invalid setup, not security findings.

OIDC provider token exchange requires redirect_uri to exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, assert rejection by status code; do not interpret failure as identity confusion.

Vault OIDC provider public clients must use PKCE. The authorization endpoint documents code_challenge as required for public clients, and the token endpoint documents code_verifier as required for public clients and for PKCE-granted codes. For public-client tests, absence of PKCE should be treated as expected rejection, not a bug.

Vault OIDC provider confidential clients may use PKCE optionally, but public clients do not have a client secret and use token endpoint auth method 'none'. When testing code exchange behavior, ensure client_type and client authentication method are consistent with the client configuration or failures will be setup artifacts.

The OIDC provider discovery document states request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against Vault's OIDC provider endpoints because request JWT objects are not supported there; any rejection is by unsupported feature, not request-object signature validation.

Client redirect_uris on Vault OIDC provider clients must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Wildcards are not documented. For flow-coherence tests, use exact registered URIs only.

OIDC provider clients default to allowing no Vault entities unless assignments are configured. To permit authentication through a client in test setup, create the client with assignments including the built-in allow_all assignment or a specific assignment resource containing the target entity/group IDs. Otherwise authorization failures are expected setup behavior.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on providers is exact list membership with a special '*' sentinel meaning all clients are allowed. Empty allowed_client_ids means no clients are allowed. Do not interpret empty as unconstrained.
OIDC provider and named key allowed_client_ids use a special sentinel: empty list means no clients are allowed, '*' means all clients are allowed. Never assume an empty list is permissive.
KV v2 verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource paths MUST include the /data/ segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns misleading 404s.

KV v2 max_versions has a sentinel meaning: value 0 does not mean keep zero versions; it means use the default retention of 10 versions. delete_version_after also has a sentinel: '0s' means no automatic deletion delay. Never assume zero means immediate deletion or no retention.

Identity group policy application mode can change authorization semantics across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace group-policy escalation tests must account for this global mode or they will misclassify documented behavior as an I5 violation.

JWT auth roles require at least one bound value. create_auth_role MUST set at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use the default 60 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict checking.
Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict expiration enforcement.
Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway value 0 means use the default 150 seconds, not literal zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict not-before enforcement.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_subject supports exact string match only. There is no companion bound_subject_type. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely; setting it to '*' matches only the literal string '*'.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_audiences is exact audience membership matching only. There is no wildcard or type parameter. For cross-provider or multi-identity scenarios, do not use '*' as a wildcard audience; omit or set explicit allowed audiences only.

Parameter matching semantics: user_claim is a claim selector, not a matcher. The selected claim value must be a string and becomes the alias name. For I4 tests, vary the underlying claim value, not the selector.

Parameter matching semantics: groups_claim is a claim selector, not a matcher. The selected claim value must be a list of strings and becomes group alias names. For I5 group-policy tests, send groups as a JSON array of strings; a scalar string is the wrong type.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_claims uses bound_claims_type to control matching. Default bound_claims_type=string means literal exact matching; glob enables '*' wildcard matching. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, if multiple different values must pass the same claim constraint, either omit that bound claim or explicitly use bound_claims_type=glob. Do not set bound_claims value '*' under default string mode because it matches only the literal '*'.

Claim value types: bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list of strings as configured values. Under the default bound_claims_type=string, values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type=glob rather than the default string so numeric JWT claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

For I5 numeric type-coercion testing on bound_claims, Vault documents integer and boolean accepted bound values. The fuzzer SHOULD test coercion by configuring an integer bound value N and sending a JWT claim with float N+0.7. Use bound_claims_type=glob if needed to avoid outright type rejection and expose silent coercion/truncation behavior.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses on JWT roles limits total uses of the issued Vault token across the entire sequence, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the fuzzer performs both a self-lookup and a protected-read after login, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated call occurs.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT login, include a control login in the same scenario using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub={{jwt_sub}}). Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust configuration or role setup.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, modify_role_config MUST tighten an existing role constraint or permissions set. Do not remove bound_claims or widen audiences during the second step, because that broadens access and invalidates the oracle.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation to replace the trusted key source. Acceptance of old keys may persist until JWKS cache refresh behavior completes when using remote JWKS; only flag stale acceptance after the documented cache behavior has been accounted for.
For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role only when configure_jwt_validation.default_role is set. If default_role is unset, the login request must include role explicitly.

OIDC provider authorize endpoint requires scope to include openid and response_type=code. For public clients, code_challenge and code_verifier are required; for confidential clients they are optional.

OIDC provider token endpoint requires redirect_uri to exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was issued. For public clients, client_id and code_verifier are required because there is no client secret.

OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint; request JWT objects are not supported there.

OIDC provider discovery reports token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported includes client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, and none. The fuzzer MUST choose an auth method consistent with client_type: confidential clients use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post; public clients use none and PKCE.

Vault OIDC provider strongly encourages nonce on authorize requests and returns it in the ID token. For replay-sensitive OIDC tests, always send a nonce and verify it in the returned id_token; omitting nonce weakens the test and may create false conclusions about replay handling.
KV v2 paths are versioned APIs. verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource MUST use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; omitting /data/ hits the wrong API shape and causes false 404/permission failures.
KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions value 0 does not mean keep zero versions; it means use Vault's default retention of 10 versions. Never interpret 0 as immediate deletion.
KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: delete_version_after value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer, not immediate deletion. Do not use 0s expecting instant expiry behavior.

Identity group behavior: external groups are intended to receive membership through aliases from auth methods. For JWT/OIDC group mapping tests, prefer type=external groups plus create_group_alias rather than manually populating member_entity_ids, so group-policy behavior reflects external claim mapping.

Group policy application mode can change authorization semantics across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies may apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. I5 group-policy escalation tests must account for this global mode before treating cross-namespace policy reach as a bug.

Every JWT/OIDC role requires at least one bound value. create_auth_role MUST set at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or other documented bound constraints; otherwise role creation/update is invalid.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway value 0 does NOT mean zero leeway; it means use the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 is strict.
Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway value 0 does NOT mean zero leeway; it means use the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 is strict.
Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway value 0 does NOT mean zero leeway; it means use the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 is strict.

bound_audiences is exact audience membership matching only; the docs define it as a list of aud claims to match and provide no wildcard/mode parameter. For cross-identity or cross-provider scenarios, do NOT use '*' as a wildcard audience. To allow multiple different audiences in one role, provide explicit values or omit the constraint when the test requires unconstrained audiences.

bound_claims matching semantics depend on bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type=string means literal exact matching only; '*' is a literal asterisk, not a wildcard. For wildcard tests, set bound_claims_type=glob explicitly. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, if different claim values must all pass, OMIT the exact-match bound claim instead of setting it to '*'.

For I5 numeric coercion tests on bound_claims, set bound_claims_type=glob, not the default string mode. The docs state string mode treats values as literals and exact matches, while glob mode interprets values as globs; use glob mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.

bound_claims accepts expected values of string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. The fuzzer SHOULD test numeric coercion explicitly: configure a numeric bound_claim value N, then send a JWT claim with float N+0.7 and observe whether Vault truncates/coerces silently. Use bound_claims_type=glob when needed to avoid outright type rejection.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. If the selected claim is absent or non-string, login will not produce the intended alias/entity mapping. For I4 tests, choose a string-valued claim such as sub and keep its type stable across variants.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Sending a scalar string where a list is expected changes behavior and can invalidate group-alias tests. For I5 group-policy tests, ensure the JWT groups claim is encoded as an array of strings.

token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued Vault token, and EVERY API call made with that session consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence needs both self-lookup and a protected-resource read, token_num_uses MUST be at least 2; use at least 3 if any extra session inspection call is included.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT in the same setup (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub={{jwt_sub}}). Without a control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken trust configuration or role setup.

For I3 jwt_role_config_tighten_reauth tests, the second login MUST be a NEW login after modify_role_config on the same role. Vault documents that role constraints are applied at login time; a valid test checks whether re-login under tightened config is rejected, not whether an already-issued token changes retroactively.

For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation to trust only the new key source, then perform a NEW login with the old JWT. Acceptance of the new trust anchor after admin reconfiguration is by design; only continued acceptance of the old key after rotation is relevant.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, omit the role parameter on login_with_jwt so Vault uses default_role. If role is supplied explicitly, changing default_role has no effect and the test is invalid.

OIDC provider client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization and token requests. For code-flow tests against Vault's OIDC provider, create_application-equivalent client setup must register the exact callback URI used later, or the flow fails for configuration reasons.
oidc_jwt.source: secret/identity/oidc-provider.mdx Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault OIDC provider clients default to allowing NO entities unless assignments are configured. Client assignments limit which Vault entities/groups may authenticate, and by default no Vault entities are allowed. For OIDC provider flow tests, configure assignments or use the built-in allow_all assignment, otherwise authorization failures are expected setup errors.
oidc_jwt.source: secret/identity/oidc-provider.mdx Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider is deny-by-default: if empty, no clients are allowed; '*' allows all clients. For cross-client tests, do not leave allowed_client_ids empty or every authorization attempt will fail for configuration reasons.
oidc_jwt.source: secret/identity/oidc-provider.mdx Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault's OIDC provider authorization endpoint documents nonce as optional but strongly encouraged. For replay-sensitive OIDC tests, the fuzzer MUST send a nonce in start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token carries the same nonce after exchange_code_for_token.

Public OIDC provider clients MUST use PKCE. The authorization endpoint requires code_challenge for public clients, and the token endpoint requires code_verifier for public clients. Do not interpret failures without PKCE on public clients as security bugs; they are required behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: secret/identity/oidc-provider.mdx Create or update a client; Authorization endpoint; Token endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: Confidential OIDC provider clients may authenticate with client_secret_basic or client_secret_post; public clients use none. When testing token exchange/code exchange behavior, choose the client authentication method consistent with client_type or failures will be due to client auth mismatch, not security enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: secret/identity/oidc-provider.mdx Create or update a client; Token endpoint

oidc_jwt.constraint: KV v2 read/write paths MUST include the /data/ segment. For verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource, use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; using the KV v1-style path will return 404 and create false negatives.

Identity group type matters for membership management. External groups are intended to receive membership via aliases from auth methods; for JWT groups-claim mapping tests, create_identity_group SHOULD use type='external' and membership should be driven by create_group_alias rather than manual member_entity_ids.

Group policy application mode can broaden effective permissions across namespaces. If /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy. I5 tests involving identity groups MUST account for this global mode or they may misclassify cross-namespace policy inheritance as escalation.
